newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up led by Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up led by Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Monday led by real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development, while the domestic A share index rose sharply on bullish sentiment, brokers said.
The B index rose 1.172 points or 1.67 percent to 71.292 points on volume of 20.4 million shares worth $9.2 million against $6.2 million last Friday.
The A share index gained 25.863 points or 2.12 percent to 1,248.299 points on turnover of 12.3 billion yuan, compared with last Friday's 8.4 billion yuan.

Brokers said institutional buying of market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui and other Pudong shares lent firm support to the market, but follow-up buying was not active as uncertainty surrounding the company reporting season prevailed.
Shanghai Lujiazui was the most active share, ending up $0.042 or 4.46 percent to $0.982 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
"Market sentiment is good in line with the recent strong performance in the domestic A share market, so a little speculative buying could push the index up," one broker said.
"The index will rise further in the short term after consolidating for days if there is no big negative news," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 28 up, three flat and 12 down.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the star on talk it would post good 1996 results soon, rising $0.05 or 6.66 percent to $0.80 on volume of 144,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share index continued to rise in active trading on bullish sentiment, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index soared 157.461 points or 4.8 percent to 3441.166 points.
Shanxi Coking was the star on speculative institutional buying late in the session, surging 1.33 yuan or 10 percent to its daily limit-up of 14.59 yuan on volume of 7.7 million shares.
